_comment: Numbers and small rules both clients use. The disk-space and keypoint-divisor values are StarCore's, which the desktop copies by hand (WorkingLocation.PEAK_TO_INPUT_RATIO, KeypointDivisor): the gui's test reads this file against StarCore's own values (DiskSpaceCheck.peakToInputRatio, Config.recommendedReducedKeypointDivisor, the presets and limits the startup prompt offers) and the desktop's against its copies, so a change in StarCore fails the gui test until this file says the same, and then the desktop test until its copy does. customFrameRate is the render sheet's custom frame rate field, which each client implements: the same cases go through both.

cleanMethod.comment: P6: the settings sheet asks Automatic or Selective, and (expert) Selective Auto Clean Yes or No. `cases` is StarCore's CleanMethod(highLevelCleanMethod:autoPreservationMode:); `autoPreservationStart` is where Selective Auto Clean stands when the sheet opens on a method.

texts.comment: The catalogue keys under the two rows: the choice's title, its hover text, and the paragraph under the row's (i). Both clients read these.

settingsTabs.comment: The tabs of the processing settings sheet, in the order both clients show them, and the one it opens on. An id is the end of the catalogue key `settings_tab.<id>` that names the tab and of the UI id `settings.tab.<id>` (gherkin/ui/ids.json) that a test finds it by.
